Influence of Different Configurations of Pt Supported on AlV‑Rich
ASA on Their Catalytic Performance in Chemoselective
Hydrogenation Evaluated by DFT Modeling and Experimental
Validation

ABSTRACT: The structure of metal nanocatalysts based on single
metal atoms (SA), subnanoclusters (NC), and nanoparticles (NP)
plays a vital role in governing their catalytic performance. Here, we
investigated the effect of different structural configurations of Pt
(PtSA, PtNC, and PtNP) supported on penta-coordinated Al (AlV)-
enriched amorphous silica−alumina (ASA) on the selective
hydrogenation of aromatic saturated and unsaturated ketones and
aldehydes. The predictive information gained by spin-polarized
density functional theory (DFT) calculations of the reaction
pathways was validated by pertinent catalytic reaction tests. Based
on the calculated apparent energy barriers and reaction pathways, a
qualitative prediction of the suitability of the different structural
configurations of Pt is given for the hydrogenation of specific
ketones and aldehydes. For the hydrogenation of aromatic saturated ketones, acetophenone and butyrophenone, the order of the
activity is NP > SA > NC. For the saturated aldehydes, benzaldehyde and phenylacetaldehyde, the corresponding order is NP > NC
> SA, and for the α,β-unsaturated aldehydes, cinnamaldehyde and benzylideneacetone, it is SA > NC > NP. PtNP favors C�O bond
over the C�C bond hydrogenation but exhibits low selectivity to the unsaturated alcohol due to consecutive hydrogenation. The
validation of the theoretically predicted results by corresponding experimental tests indicates good qualitative agreement between
theoretical and experimental results. The combined strategy based on predictive DFT analysis and experimental validation offers an
interesting approach for designing and optimizing catalysts.
KEYWORDS: structural configuration, AlV-enriched amorphous silica−alumina, chemoselective hydrogenation,
DFT prediction of reaction pathways, reaction energy profiles
